ex_jump_squat_weighted.description: Loaded jump squat for explosive leg power — direct pop-up and turn drive.
techniqueCues: Light load on back (barbell, vest, or dumbbells)
Quarter squat, then explode up — arms drive for momentum
Land soft, absorb through hips and knees
Reset posture before the next rep — don't rush fatigued jumps
ex_jump_squat_weighted.injuryNotes: Keep load light; this is power work, not max strength. Skip if knees are irritated.

ex_kneeling_jump_squat.description: Barbell jump from kneeling — builds explosive hip drive for pop-ups and committed turns.
techniqueCues: Bar racked on upper back; kneel with hips back to heels
Chest up, brace core, then explode hips to land on both feet
Absorb softly and finish standing in a full squat
Reset kneeling between reps — quality over speed
ex_kneeling_jump_squat.injuryNotes: Advanced plyometric with load; start bodyweight or empty bar. Skip if knees are sore.

ex_hevy_4f5866f8.description: Low-back emphasis on the 45° bench — erector endurance for upright paddle posture.
techniqueCues: Pad support over the hips — hip crease at the top edge of the pad
Rise straight in one line — minimal hip hinge, torso stays rigid
Arms crossed or plate held tight to the chest
Stop at neutral; don't over-arch at the top
ex_hevy_4f5866f8.injuryNotes: If you feel sharp lumbar pain, lower the pad or switch to the glute setup.

ex_hevy_091737fa.description: Loaded low-back hyperextension — builds erector strength for long paddle sessions.
techniqueCues: Pad over the hips, same straight-torso setup as bodyweight low-back version
Hold the plate tight to your chest — load stays close to the body
Rise in a straight line; squeeze erectors, not glutes
Lower with control — no bouncing at the bottom
ex_hevy_091737fa.injuryNotes: Start light; this targets the lower back directly under load.

ex_hyperextension_glutes.description: Glute emphasis on the 45° bench — hip extension power for pop-ups and turn drive.
techniqueCues: Pad lower — support down on the hips, more thigh on the pad
Rise with a small spinal curve — squeeze glutes hard at the top
Arms extended or plate held away from the body
Hinge at the hips on the way down; feel the stretch in hamstrings
ex_hyperextension_glutes.injuryNotes: A slight arch at the top is intentional here — keep it small and glute-driven, not lumbar snap.

ex_weighted_hyperextension_glutes.description: Loaded glute hyperextension — posterior-chain power with the weight as a long lever.
techniqueCues: Pad low on the hips — same glute-bias setup as the bodyweight version
Hold the plate with arms extended — weight far from the body
Drive up with a small spinal curve, glutes doing the work
Lower until hamstrings stretch; don't collapse through the lower back
ex_weighted_hyperextension_glutes.injuryNotes: The long lever increases demand — build load slowly and keep the arch glute-led.

ex_hevy_6a6c31a5.description: Wide-grip cable lat pulldown — builds the vertical pull strength behind paddle power.
techniqueCues: Thighs pinned under the pad, slight lean back, shoulders down
Pull the bar to upper chest — elbows drive down and slightly back
Squeeze lats at the bottom; think paddle catch
Control the return; don't let the stack yank your shoulders up
ex_hevy_6a6c31a5.injuryNotes: Avoid behind-the-neck pulldowns — pull to the front of the chest only.

ex_hevy_867ac3b6.description: Feet-up (Larsen) bench press — strict chest press with legs off the floor, removing leg drive for pure pressing strength.
techniqueCues: Lie on the bench with legs extended — feet off the floor (flying feet)
Shoulder blades pinned, slight arch, bar to mid-chest
Press without using leg drive or hip bridge
Control the descent — this exposes weak points in your chest press
ex_hevy_867ac3b6.injuryNotes: Use less weight than your regular bench; the strict setup loads the shoulders and chest differently.

ex_hevy_f72fa239.description: Dumbbell squeeze press — constant inward pressure on the bells for inner-chest and triceps work.
techniqueCues: Lie back with dumbbells squeezed together over your chest, neutral grip
Keep pressing the bells into each other throughout the rep
Lower to mid-chest, then press up and slightly inward
Shoulders pinned — don't let elbows flare wide
ex_hevy_f72fa239.injuryNotes: Use moderate weight; the squeeze fatigues wrists and forearms faster than a normal press.

ex_hevy_651f844c.description: High-pulley cable crossover — upper chest and anterior delt squeeze from a standing fly.
techniqueCues: Pulleys set high, step forward into a stable staggered stance
Slight bend in elbows, arms sweep down and in toward your hips
Squeeze chest hard at the bottom — knuckles meet in front
Control the stretch on the way back; don't let cables pull your shoulders forward
ex_hevy_651f844c.injuryNotes: Start light — the long lever at high pulleys stresses the shoulder capsule if you rush the stretch.

ex_hevy_c315dc2a.description: High-pulley cable crossover for shoulders — rear delt and upper-back focus, paired with the chest crossover.
techniqueCues: Pulleys set high, cross handles in front at shoulder height
Arms stay mostly straight — pull back and out, not down to the hips
Squeeze rear delts and mid-back at the end range
Control the return; don't let the stack wrench your shoulders forward
ex_hevy_c315dc2a.injuryNotes: Keep weight light — this is isolation work for shoulder health and posture, not max loading.

ex_hevy_de68c825.description: Single-arm cable lateral raise from a low pulley — targets the side delt for shoulder width and paddle stability.
techniqueCues: Low pulley, stand sideways — free hand on the frame for balance
Slight bend in the working elbow, cable crosses in front of your body at the start
Raise your arm out to the side until wrist and elbow are at shoulder height
Lower with control; switch sides after each set
ex_hevy_de68c825.injuryNotes: Don't shrug the trap or swing — if you need momentum, the weight is too heavy.

ex_hevy_2dbca395.description: Bayesian (behind-the-back) cable curl — elbows behind the torso for a deep bicep stretch and long-head emphasis.
techniqueCues: Low pulley behind you, handles in hand, step forward so arms trail behind your hips
Staggered stance, chest up, elbows fixed behind your torso
Curl without letting elbows drift forward — squeeze at the top
Lower slowly for a full stretch behind the body
ex_hevy_2dbca395.injuryNotes: Start light — the stretched position loads the bicep tendon; avoid swinging or heaving the weight.

ex_hevy_234897ab.description: Neutral-grip cable hammer curl with a rope — brachialis and forearm strength for paddle grip and board carry.
techniqueCues: Low pulley with rope, neutral grip (palms facing each other)
Elbows pinned to your sides, shoulders back
Curl the rope to chest height without swinging
Lower with control — full extension at the bottom
ex_hevy_234897ab.injuryNotes: Keep wrists neutral; don't let elbows drift forward on the curl.
